reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows net interest income after the tax-equivalent adjustment rising while total interest expense fell and total fees and commissions rose; the tax-equivalent adjustment itself was essentially unchanged, so the net interest income move is not a tax-bridge artifact. Average earning assets declined over the same sequential period, so the net interest income improvement is consistent with a higher spread on a smaller balance sheet rather than volume growth, but the selected rows contain no yield, rate, mix, deposit-cost or credit detail, so no causal driver is established. Fee income growth is a separate revenue line and is not evidence about spread. The thesis is a source-bounded baseline with no valuation or conviction claim attached, and the selected rows do not contradict its assumptions; the research state is therefore maintained rather than upgraded, with conviction unchanged. Material counterevidence: the shrinking average earning asset base means the earnings improvement is not volume-supported and could reverse if spread compression returns. Missing evidence that would change the view: net interest margin and yield/cost decomposition, noninterest expense and provision detail, GAAP net income and diluted EPS, company-defined non-GAAP measures, and any forward guidance, none of which are in this extract; their absence from the extract is not evidence of their absence from the filing. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic, not year-over-year and not causal attribution.
